per_policy_guidance.guidance: Lower-priority specialist, not a default: it passed the final skill exit in 5/12 in-distribution runs. Its object-frame target prior is intended for reliable block-position displacement, but that benefit has no out-of-distribution validation. Use only with drawer open/stable, a reliable low block pose, and an open gripper free of the handle; prefer h02 for a near-nominal block with unusual TCP/configuration and h03 when low-clearance ordering is the concern. Avoid with noisy/dropped object pose, displaced tunnel/drawer, or questionable reachability/collision clearance. Monitor for fingers closing without persistent object/TCP coupling, an open gripper, a low/stationary block, premature low transfer, drawer falling to <=0.26, or repeated IK nonconvergence/limit contacts. Validation showed nonzero IK-unconverged steps in 10/12 runs, and all seven final failures had an earlier first-pass step, so do not treat a transient exit observation as maintained success. Hand off in the supervised 680:840 overlap only after the block is outside the tunnel with its bottom above the 0.16 m roof (or already in the drawer), drawer_position remains >0.26, closed-finger object/TCP coupling persists, and motion has turned toward target_pose.

Preferred default on states matching this policy's demonstrated segment entry: it passed 12/12 in-distribution runs, finished with drawer_position about 0.300 in every run, and reported zero IK-unconverged steps. Use with an open stable drawer, a low block near demonstrated tunnel support, finite collision-free arm state, and two causal frames retained across switching. Its fresh-TCP body-delta representation is the documented choice when a valid predecessor TCP/configuration mismatch is the main variation, but that unusual-handoff benefit itself was not exercised by the nearly fixed training entries. Avoid relying on it for large block displacement, global path/collision guarantees, or failed-grasp recovery. Detect failure from local-correction drift away from block/destination, phase oscillation, fingers closing without block/TCP coupling, failure to rise, drawer_position <=0.26, or repeated IK nonconvergence/limits. Hand off during the 680:840 overlap after persistent closed-finger coupling, tunnel exit, block-bottom clearance above 0.16 m (or block already inside), drawer_position >0.26, and destination-directed motion; closure alone is insufficient.

Preferred default when extraction/lift/transfer phase ambiguity or premature below-roof transfer is the main concern: it passed 12/12 in-distribution runs, ended with drawer_position about 0.300 throughout, and had zero IK-unconverged steps. Use only with training-like world/tunnel geometry, an open stable drawer, a valid target_pose, and a low tunnel block; its narrow guard conservatively caps destination-directed +x motion when closed-near-object proxies indicate the block is below 0.16 m. Avoid if target_pose/geometry is unreliable, if a valid unseen maneuver intentionally requires low transfer, or if failed-grasp recovery is needed; use h01 only for the unvalidated displaced-block specialization and h02 for a major valid TCP/configuration mismatch. Failure signs are closed fingers without object/TCP coupling, repeated guard intervention while the block stays low, failure to rise, drop, destination drift, drawer_position <=0.26, or persistent IK nonconvergence/limits. Hand off in 680:840 once coupling persists, the block is outside with its bottom above the roof (or already inside), drawer_position >0.26, the guard is inactive, and transfer is directed toward the drawer.

Experimental/lower-priority specialist: it passed only 4/12 in-distribution runs, so do not use it as a default or as evidence that block-displacement handling works. Its dual-reference prior is intended for reliable block translation with a correct observed destination, but neither that benefit nor the clearance blend has out-of-distribution validation. If invoked, require drawer_position >0.26 and stable, reliable object_pose/height and target_pose, a low block, and an open gripper at normal entry. Avoid rotated/displaced setups that can make block-relative targets unreachable/colliding, noisy height near the blend transition, wrong destination, or uncertain grasp recovery; prefer h02 for near-nominal block plus TCP/configuration mismatch and h03 for explicit conservative low-clearance guarding. Watch for large object/destination candidate disagreement, abrupt blend-band targets, destination motion below the roof, no extraction/lift, closed fingers without coupling, drop, drawer disturbance, or IK/limit faults. In validation all eight failures kept the drawer near 0.300 and had zero IK-unconverged steps but never reached retrieval, so an open drawer and clean IK are not sufficient progress indicators. Hand off only after persistent coupling, tunnel exit, positive block-bottom clearance above 0.16 m (or already inside), drawer_position >0.26, high destination-branch weight, and destination-directed motion; blend weight or closure alone is insufficient.

summary: Validation was strictly in distribution: each policy started from its own training-segment entry state in each of 12 training demonstrations, used its training call arguments, ran for 810 steps (1.5x the 540-step segment), and was scored only at the final state. The common skill exit is: block outside the tunnel footprint with its bottom above the 0.16 m roof (or already inside the drawer) and drawer_position >0.26. There are no out-of-distribution results. h02 and h03 are the validated first-line choices (12/12 each): select h02 for the fresh-TCP/local-correction prior and h03 when conservative extraction-before-transfer ordering is desired. h01 (5/12) and h04 (4/12) are displacement-oriented specialists whose intended displacement advantages remain unverified and whose in-distribution reliability is substantially lower. Use common call fields object_pose and target_pose with tunnel_clearance_m=0.16, preserve two-frame causal history across switches, and require observed object/TCP coupling rather than closed fingers alone. None of these validations establishes placement, drawer closing, collision safety, contact truth, or failed-grasp recovery; all recorded final full-task success flags were false, as expected for this intermediate retrieval skill.
